question: What attributes characterize the lord of will in relation to desire, form, and self-movement?
premises: The addressed lord is identified as the sovereign of will.
This will encompasses desire and related impulses while remaining partless.
The lord's own movement is described as supremely clear and self-determined.
inference: The lord of will unites manifold desire within an undivided will and manifests through a supremely clear, autonomous movement.
uncertainties: The precise meaning or referent of 'nāckahalā' in 'nāckahalākṛte' is unclear.
plain_english: O lord of will, whose will includes desire and the rest yet remains partless, who has taken the form of nāckahalā, and whose own movement is supremely clear!
